# Lacuna v0.14.3

Lacuna v0.14.3 is a correctness patch from the website documentation pass over v0.14.2, which reran
every documented example against the published packages and reported where behavior and
documentation disagreed. It preserves every v0.13 and v0.14 public signature, the schema-v1 result
envelope, c14n-v1 identities, and deterministic RNG streams.

Two corrections change a reported value and carry a new method version. The rest fix inputs that
were documented as supported and failed, or that were accepted and misread.

## Advisory: CSV time columns and quantile observation counts

**Slash-separated CSV dates were read day-first.** `lacuna signal` in v0.14.2 documented ISO 8601
time text but passed anything else to format inference. `02/01/2025` became 2 January, so a
month-first file was misdated without an error. v0.14.3 rejects text that is not ISO 8601. If you
ran `lacuna signal` in v0.14.2 on a CSV whose time column was not ISO text, rerun it after
converting the column.

**The quantile observation count pooled horizons.** v0.14.2 moved the headline spread and
monotonicity of `signal.quantiles` and `signal.bucket_returns` to one horizon but kept reporting
`n_observations` over every horizon. In method version 3 the count describes the headline horizon,
as `signal.ic` already did. Per-horizon tables are unchanged.

## Results that change

| Method | Version | What changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signal.quantiles`, `signal.bucket_returns` | method 3 | `n_observations` counts headline-horizon rows only |
| `signal.quantiles` | method 3 | An empty headline horizon is reported as `QUANTILE_HEADLINE_HORIZON_EMPTY`, not under the `BUCKET_` code |
| `bias.asof_join` | method 2 | No value changes from v0.14.2; the version its v0.14.2 changes owed |
| `bias.revision_diagnostics` | method 2 | String and categorical revisions are rejected; float and Duration revisions are accepted |

`bias.asof_join` results from v0.14.2 report method version 1 although the tolerance validation,
the revision rules, and the computed `future_matches` were already in effect. Version 2 identifies
that behavior from v0.14.3 on.

## Fixes

- **Duration in as-of joins.** `bias.asof_join` works on `Duration` time and revision columns, as
  documented. Every such call failed with a Polars cast error. Evidence records durations as
  ISO 8601 text such as `P1D`.
- **Bare label frames.** `ic`, `quantiles`, `bucket_returns`, and `decay` accept
  `labels.frame` together with a non-default `instrument=`; v0.14.2 fixed this for `LabelResult`
  input only.
- **`missing="raise"` with delisting returns.** `forward_returns(missing="raise")` accepts the null
  exit price on a row that carries a delisting return, so the two options can be combined.
- **Integer horizon policy.** `lc.audit(policies={"inference_horizon": 5})` reads the `"5D"`
  horizon, as `SignalStudy.audit` does. It matched nothing, which made the horizon rules `UNKNOWN`
  and kept the zero-purge warning from firing.

## Migration

Inputs that are now rejected:

- `lacuna signal`: CSV time text that is not `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD`, `T` or a space, then
  `HH:MM[:SS[.fraction]]` with an optional `Z` or numeric UTC offset.
- `bias.revision_diagnostics`: string or categorical `revision` columns (cast to an integer or an
  ordered Enum).

Results to read differently:

- Code that reads `n_observations` from `quantiles` or `bucket_returns` with multi-horizon labels
  gets the headline horizon's count. The total over horizons is the sum of the per-horizon tables;
  `matched_rows_before_policy` still covers every matched row.
- Code that looks for `BUCKET_HEADLINE_HORIZON_EMPTY` in a `quantiles` result must look for
  `QUANTILE_HEADLINE_HORIZON_EMPTY`.

## Closed without a code change

- `fit_decay` records `root_entropy` only when resampling runs. A result that stops at a support
  or direction gate draws no random numbers; the signal guide now says so.
- `regime.analysis` stays at method version 1: its v0.14.2 change added a recorded parameter and a
  warning and changed no value.
- `lacuna-options` `validate_chain` accepts an input column named `delta_bucket`; the collision
  check is in `delta_buckets`, as the 0.2.2 changelog states.

## `lacuna-options`

Unchanged at 0.2.2. It remains compatible with `lacuna-quant>=0.13,<0.15`.

## Verification

Each fix has a regression test that fails on v0.14.2. The benchmark cases that carry
`signal.quantiles` evidence change their output checksums because of the count correction; they are
recorded in the performance guide.
